title: CrowdStrike Extends the Agentic SOC to Detect and Stop Agent Insider Threats
summary: CrowdStrike extends the agentic SOC to detect agent insider threats, investigate across every domain, and govern response on the Falcon platform.
body_markdown:
The most dangerous agent in your environment may be one you already approved.


It runs under a real employee's identity, connects to tools their team signed off on, and has the access it needs to do its job. But when something upstream changes, like a tampered tool or an instruction that shouldn't be there, it can drift without tripping an alarm. This is the new insider threat: not an employee, but a trusted agent acting on their behalf.


AI agents touch the SOC in two ways: They’re the new operating unit of the SOC and a new identity to secure. Two categories of tools are being sold against these realities, but they fall short in different ways. Most agentic SOC tools run a single LLM serially through detections, with no memory of prior investigations or identity, endpoint, or ownership context — so they can't tell a routine action from a compromise. Standalone AI security tools can inventory agents and flag unusual activity, but they stop at detection, handing the problem to another tool while the agent keeps running.


Today, CrowdStrike is advancing the agentic SOC to do both through the CrowdStrike Falcon[®](https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/platform/falcon-guardian-aidr/) platform so teams can secure the agents running in their environment and put expert agents to work inside the SOC to investigate and respond to threats at machine speed.


Figure 1. Agentic Investigations brings specialist agents together on shared context to investigate across domains and converge on one verdict


## Introducing Insider Threat Detection


Security teams face hundreds of thousands of alerts a month, and agents add more telemetry. An agent insider threat rarely sounds a loud alarm. On their own, the signs look like something an AI coding agent does every day. Spread across separate alerts, they're easy to dismiss. Taken together and tied to the same agent, person, and machine, they tell a different story.


**Agent Insider Threat Detection (Q4)** is built to see that story. CrowdStrike Falcon® Next-Gen SIEM learns the normal behavior pattern for every AI agent and the person who runs it, the files it touches, the tools it calls, and where it sends data, and flags deviations even when no policy is violated. That's how it catches the agent that stays within its granted permissions and is still compromised.


Figure 2. Understand the full risk picture


When individual signals are brought together, a clear picture forms. With **Dynamic Risk Scoring (Q4)** , agent risk feeds into the same 0 to 100 risk score that Falcon Next-Gen SIEM already builds for the agent's owner and host. When an agent, its user, and its device all climb the risk list together, the coordination behind otherwise routine activity is harder to miss.


This foundation extends to the place many of these attacks begin: the AI tooling agents depend on. **AI Ecosystem Detections (Q4)** add detection logic for attacks on AI services, including LLM API abuse, stolen API keys, and the compromise of coding assistants, MCP servers, and agent frameworks. When the threat starts in a trusted tool rather than the agent itself, the Falcon platform is watching there too.


Because the context around an agent doesn't always live inside the Falcon platform, **Federated Search Expansion** lets teams search related data where it already lives, without re-ingestion. New connectors for GovCloud, Dynatrace, Databricks, and Snowflake are now generally available, with Splunk, Elastic, and Cribl Lake connectors following in Q4.


## Act on Tough Questions


Once a risky agent surfaces, every analyst faces the same question: Did an agent’s owner do this, or did their agent do it without them knowing?


This is the work **Multi-Agent Triage and Investigation (GA,[announced at Fal.Con US](https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/crowdstrike-delivers-next-evolution-of-agentic-soc) 2026)** was built for. SOC agents investigate detections end to end, with specialist agents working the case together on shared context across endpoint, identity, and the agent's activity.


Investigation coverage already spans the full range of Falcon platform and third-party sources. In Q4, triage coverage extends to CrowdStrike Falcon® Guardian, CrowdStrike Falcon® Cloud Security, CrowdStrike Falcon® Shield, CrowdStrike Falcon® Data Security, and custom detections, including abnormal agent behavior flagged by Falcon Next-Gen SIEM. When an agent is flagged, it routes straight into an agentic investigation where the agent, its owner, and its host are already connected.


This shared context is what answers the tough question. Investigating agents can trace a session back to what the person asked for and separate it from what the agent did on its own. When the person's request was routine and everything that followed traces to instructions they never wrote, the verdict becomes clear: The insider was the agent, not the employee.


But a verdict doesn't stop a compromised agent that's still running. The **Unified Agentic SOAR Experience (GA, announced at Fal.Con US 2026)** is where response happens. Teams build, run, and govern all automation in the SOC, from AI agents to workflows to custom apps, in plain language. They set the mission and define triggers, data, rules, and actions to decide what runs autonomously and what requires approval. A single response decision can coordinate everything that needs to follow in parallel: stopping the agent, cutting off its access, keeping it from coming back, and documenting what happened. It's open by design and connects to any agent, model, or tool through API or MCP, so teams can govern automation across the security stack with visibility into what it's costing and what needs attention.

## Autonomy That Earns Its Trust


As SOCs hand more of the work to agents, the controls that keep agents accountable matter as much as the speed they deliver.


CrowdStrike builds governance into every layer of the agentic SOC. It starts by watching the SOC's agents. **Policy-Drift Agent Guardrails, powered by Falcon Guardian (Beta, Q4)** , screen every CrowdStrike Charlotte AI™ and AgentWorks interaction for policy drift, unauthorized tool calls, and out-of-bounds data access to catch the moment an agent steps outside its intended scope.


Figure 3. Human-in-the-Loop Action Requests let analysts approve or reject a sensitive agent action before it runs.


When an agent reaches for something sensitive, a human makes the call. **Human-in-the-Loop Action Requests (GA)** pause a Falcon-native or AgentWorks agent the moment it invokes a sensitive tool and raise an Action Request. Analysts approve, reject with a documented reason, or inspect the full agent trace before anything runs.


**Approvals for Agents and Workflows (Q4)** extends that same gate from a single tool call to an entire agent, app, or workflow, so teams can require sign-off before a whole automation runs. **Agent Interruption (GA)** lets analysts pause or stop a running SOC agent mid-task, preventing unauthorized action and runaway spend once an agent is already in motion. Finally, AI Credit Visibility and Control (Q4) gives admins real-time visibility into the credits every SOC agent and workflow consumes, the ability to halt consumption mid-run, and approval over raising a limit when an agent hits its cap.


## Why This Only Works on the Falcon Platform


**One connected picture of the agent, identity, and host** : CrowdStrike's commander-and-sub-agent framework shares memory and context across every investigation, running in parallel to work through the detection backlog so analysts only see the ones that need human judgment. This shared context is also what exposes an agent behaving like an insider, because identity, runtime activity, and endpoint telemetry are already connected rather than scattered across disconnected tools.


**Agents trained by industry-leading SOC analysts** : CrowdStrike's agents have seen it before, because they're built on CrowdStrike Falcon® Complete's operational knowledge from tens of thousands of global customers. This foundation drives more accurate and cost-effective results than a general-purpose model can on its own.


**Coverage from detection to response** : Knowing an agent has gone rogue doesn't help if the team can't act on it. CrowdStrike covers the full lifecycle on one platform: Detect through behavioral baselining, investigate through multi-agent parallelized analysis, and respond directly across the endpoint and the entire security stack, with nothing handed off between disconnected tools.


The agentic enterprise runs on trust in the agents acting on employees' behalf. CrowdStrike's agentic SOC is built to verify it: detecting threats, uncovering intent, and coordinating response across agents, identities, and endpoints.
